function.name: done
function.arguments: {"summary": "Task not completed. The red block was successfully grasped and carried twice, but the grip (a corner-grip at a 34-degree yaw) slipped during a yaw adjustment and the block dropped back onto the table. A second grasp and carry released it just short of the bowl; the block now rests on the table against the outside of the bowl wall, not inside it. The wrist camera is offset toward the forearm and the jaw-opening reading stays near zero even when holding, which made grip verification unreliable.", "hindsight": "The wrist camera is mounted proximal to the yaw joint and offset toward the forearm: the block appears between the jaws even when the gripper is centimeters off, and the apparent finger position shifts with yaw, so wrist-view alignment is unreliable for fine aiming; cross-check against the fixed front/side cameras instead. The measured gripper value is not a hold indicator: it reads near 0.02 both when closing empty and when holding the block, because the jaws press past it; verify a hold by whether the block disappears (occluded) from the wrist view or by lifting and watching the fixed cameras. Arm motion only progresses during gripper-stroke windows (about 40-80 steps, roughly 5-6mm of arm travel per step); without a gripper state change, each call advances only about 1.5-1.8cm, so pair every long motion with a gripper command when possible, and avoid large yaw swings while holding a block in a corner-grip - it flings the block out."}
